name: Packet Digital
old_description: Building Smarter Batteries and Power Products in the United States
about:
Packet Digital is based in Fargo, North Dakota. Founded in 2003, the company began as a developer of power-saving computer chips before expanding into wireless tracking systems for agriculture and logistics. The founders are not named in the source material.

Today the company designs, manufactures, assembles, and tests smart batteries and power systems for unmanned aerial systems (UAS). Operations span a 25,000-square-foot battery pack manufacturing and assembly facility equipped with a surface-mount technology line, laser welders, and thermal chambers, plus an 80,000-square-foot battery cell manufacturing campus under the Badland Batteries subsidiary that broke ground in 2024. The firm has produced runs such as 10,000 printed circuit boards for an agricultural technology customer.

Customers include the U.S. Marines, U.S. Navy, Air Force Research Laboratory, and commercial UAS platforms worldwide. The company also serves the space sector with power components for CubeSats and the agriculture technology sector through partners like 701x, which uses GPS-enabled smart ear tags for cattle management.

Packet Digital emphasizes U.S.-based production, claiming the first battery factory in North Dakota and the first in the United States to manufacture cells specifically for drones and unmanned systems. Its smart batteries integrate real-time monitoring of state of charge, cell temperature, and fault reporting to extend flight time and improve safety. The company holds CMMC Level 2 certification for defense work.
